headline: South Asia: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen.
- India: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
- Western Russia: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
Ret. Army Gen. David Petraeus praised the Pentagon’s new Autonomous Warfare Command but said the U.S. must rapidly prepare for modern autonomous war.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
- Jamaica Gleaner, one day ago: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
Government senator Marlon Morgan has called for the reintroduction of criminal sanctions for defamation in Jamaica. Making his contribution to the State of the Nation Debate in the Upper House on Friday, Morgan took aim at the parliamentary Opposition and those he referred to as their surrogates and supporters on social media, blasting them for tarnishing people’s reputation. He warned that the misinformation and disinformation being peddled by these persons serve to undermine the country’s democracy.
- Jamaica Gleaner, one day ago: PATHWAYS MURDER TRIAL | Second JP backs claim Ruddock was not forced to give statement.
A second justice of the peace (JP) on Friday testified that Andre Ruddock voluntarily gave police a statement in which he allegedly confessed to cutting Taneka Gardner’s throat. The witness corroborated earlier testimony from a colleague that Ruddock was not forced, threatened or harmed, nor offered any inducement to give the caution statement, on October 18, 2021 – a day after Gardner was killed in an alleged sacrificial ritual at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James.
- Jamaica Gleaner, one day ago: What to know about AI-detected Internet security bug.
AP: The language that’s known as the backbone of the Internet is now subject to what experts describe as one of the most notable vulnerabilities in recent memory. PHP is a widely used general-purpose scripting language that is geared toward web development, and thus, it powers the majority of websites around the world. When the organisation behind the language and the Federal Bureau of Investigations’ cyber division warned Wednesday of significant vulnerabilities in the language, government agencies, corporations and other organisations were sent into a flurry.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Messi wins Princess of Asturias award for sporting, humanitarian work.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 2 days ago: Messi wins Princess of Asturias award for sporting, humanitarian work.
The 2022 World Cup winner, the first Argentine athlete to receive the prize, said his late father was ‘very excited about’ the award La entrada Messi wins Princess of Asturias award for sporting, humanitarian work se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Four killed and 14 injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast – video.
Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast killed four people and injured 14, including an 11-year-old girl.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Three firefighters injured in Russian attacks on Kharkiv – photo.
Russian forces attacked Kharkiv with drones on the evening of 24 October. Four people, including three firefighters, were injured in the strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russian drone strikes apartment building in Vinnytsia: six injured, four flats destroyed – photos.
A Russian drone hit a five-storey apartment building in Vinnytsia, injuring six people and destroying four flats.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Russian forces strike critical infrastructure in Dnipro.
Russian forces have attacked critical infrastructure in the city of Dnipro.
Southern Europe: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iraq braces for renewed Iran conflict after 1,000 strikes on Kurdistan, 600 militia attacks.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Iraq braces for renewed Iran conflict after 1,000 strikes on Kurdistan, 600 militia attacks.
Baghdad shut crossings with Iran this week, and the Kurdistan Region denied hosting Ukrainian drones, as Iraq moves to avoid being drawn into another round of fighting.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Trump mocks reporter asking about Iran strikes, as Tehran says US derailed.
US President Donald Trump sarcastically responded to a reporter asking about possible renewed attacks on Iran.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Netanyahu shares AI-generated image of nuclear explosion in Tel Aviv, two days before election.
The prime minister's Instagram post, warning of Iran's nuclear threat, drew criticism from opposition leaders Yair Golan and Gadi Eisenkot, who accused him of using fear as an election tactic.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: High Court strikes down petition to end sperm donor anonymity.
With technology already eroding donor secrecy, petitioners asked the court to recognize a child’s right to know, as children conceived by a donor in Israel cannot learn their father’s identity
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Drone Strikes Killed At Least 306 People in Three Weeks.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 days ago: Sudan: Drone Strikes Killed At Least 306 People in Three Weeks.
[UN News] UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Friday strongly condemned an escalation in drone strikes across Sudan this month, which killed at least 306 people and injured hundreds more in the first three weeks of October alone.
- Africanews, 2 days ago: Johannesburg men run in purple briefs to raise prostate cancer awareness.
A sea of purple briefs takes over Johannesburg. Men hit the streets on Friday for the Hollard Daredevil Run, raising awareness about prostate cancer, now the most commonly diagnosed cancer in South Africa.
- Africanews, 2 days ago: Benin earns four nominations at 2026 Africa Tourism Awards.
Benin has been nominated in four categories at the 2026 Africa Tourism Awards, putting the West African nation in the spotlight for its cultural heritage and tourism appeal.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Houthis target Saudi Arabia's south as Riyadh airport due to reopen.
Yemen’s Houthi rebels launched wide-ranging strikes across swathes of southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday, as the kingdom announced the partial reopening of Riyadh’s international airport despite repeated attacks by the group. Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted. Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: The nuclear danger at sea.
Dawn’s October 23 editorial rightly warned about India’s nuclear-armed submarine patrols. The danger is larger than a new vessel at sea. It is a sea-based nuclear force growing alongside precision-strike capabilities, missile defence and a false confidence in initiating military action. Imagining that these developments confer a first-strike advantage or create a safe space for war is imprudent. Pakistan has the capability and resolve to preserve the strategic balance.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Israeli strike on university in Gaza City kills 3; another 4 Palestinians killed in separate airstrikes.
An Israeli strike on a university in Gaza City killed three people on Sunday, staff and a local hospital said, while the civil defence agency reported four others killed elsewhere in the territory. Reached for comment, the Israeli military said it was looking into the reports. Al Shifa Hospital said it received three bodies and treated eight people who were wounded in the Gaza City drone strike, with two sources at the Islamic University saying those killed were administrative staff and the injured were students.
- The Hindu - International, Times of India - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Houthis say Saudi strikes kill at least 11 after missiles intercepted.
The Houthis' Al-Masirah reported a series of "Saudi enemy airstrikes" targeting Sanaa, including one on a house that killed at least three people and wounded several others.
India - bottom line: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Trump Says "Gotta Stop" Killing Iran Leaders To Know Who US Is Dealing With.
In the first few weeks of the war, the US and Israel killed several of Iran's top political and military leaders, including Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in airstrikes.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: ‘Nuclear threat will overshadow all’: Netanyahu’s Iran warning ahead of polls.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has issued a stark warning about the looming Iranian nuclear threat. Analyst Yuval Blumberg emphasizes the urgency of the next two years for Israel to take decisive measures. He cautioned against letting internal political matters overshadow critical national security issues, especially with the parliamentary election approaching on October 27. Trump's support of Netanyahu further solidifies their alliance as essential in addressing Iran's ambitions.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: India, Australia troops train for coastal, island warfare in AUSTRAHIND 2026.
Indian and Australian army troops are actively participating in joint combat drills at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram, designated Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026. This exercise, featuring approximately 240 servicemen including 120 from each country and a New Zealand observer team, is crafted to boost operational synergy with specialized activities such as combat swimming, ambush strategies, and focused aerial operations aimed at refining skills for joint coastal and island maneuvers.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Israel elections: Can Netanyahu turn security gains into a political victory?.
Israeli voters will head to the polls on October 27 in a significant election for Benjamin Netanyahu. His political future hinges on addressing security failures following the October 7 attack by Hamas. Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a primary challenger, emphasizing military accountability over Netanyahu's leadership. The election highlights divisions within the opposition and potential coalition challenges.
Asia - bottom line: Israel widens West Bank crackdown, displacing Hebron families after attack.
- South China Morning Post - China, Taipei Times, 8 hours ago: Israel widens West Bank crackdown, displacing Hebron families after attack.
Israel said on Sunday all land crossings with the West Bank will be closed on the day of next week’s election, as it pledged a harder line on militancy after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in the territory. The announcement came a day after Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron and displaced around 2,000 residents, with Defence Minister Israel Katz saying, “they will not be allowed to return … until we’ve finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in...
- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: Gulf economies accelerate diversification as recession looms over Iran war.
Before the outbreak of the war triggered by the US-Israeli attack on Iran in February, the Gulf monarchies were living the prosperity dream that was the envy of the world. Their hydrocarbon-fuelled economies were glitzy oases of growth, inoculated from the conflict in Gaza that had rocked other parts of the Middle East for several years. Underpinned by decades-old US security guarantees and conflict mediation by billionaire sheikhs, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar cultivated...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: China’s Liaoning carrier and USS Theodore Roosevelt may be in Philippine Sea at same time.
China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier strike group sailed beyond the first island chain last week to reach the southernmost waters of the Philippines, suggesting an intent to position itself closer to ongoing US-Japan joint exercises. Philippine news channel BNC reported that the carrier group reached about 25 nautical miles (46km) east-southeast of Balut Island, the southernmost point of the Philippines, before sailing northeast on Friday. That positioned the warships past the first island chain, a...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: War of words over Xinjiang erupts between Chinese and Turkish social media users.
The debate over ethnic identity in Xinjiang has triggered an online clash between Chinese and Turkish social media users. The row began earlier this month when a Turkish social media user recalled an encounter with a Uygur from Xinjiang, the region in China that is home to nearly 12 million mainly Muslim Turkic speakers. The user wrote that the woman did not look Chinese, but when asked whether she considered herself Turkic, the woman responded: “No, I’m Chinese.” The user also called on her to...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Kim Jong Un says North Korea ‘inspired’ by China’s success in border city visit.
- NK News, 14 hours ago: Kim Jong Un says North Korea ‘inspired’ by China’s success in border city visit.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said his country is “inspired” by China’s success during a visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday marking the 76th anniversary of China entering the Korean War, according to DPRK state media. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported Sunday on Kim’s visit to the “Memorial […]

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Another Perth beach closed as more whale remains found.
- ABC News Australia, 9 hours ago: Another Perth beach closed as more whale remains found.
All beaches in Sorrento, where a man was attacked and killed by a great white shark last month, have been closed after a whale's tail was found offshore.
- The Guardian - Australia, 20 hours ago: The BoM’s temperature record keeping is under attack – again. What’s going on? | Temperature Check.
An ‘audit’ of the Bureau of Meteorology main dataset for measuring climate change claims it contains ‘widespread errors’. It doesn’t stack up Want to get this in your inbox when it publishes? Sign up for the Clear Air Australia newsletter here Australia’s climate has warmed by more than 1.5C since 1910, according to the Bureau of Meteorology’s main long-term temperature data. If you were so motivated, you might think if you could discredit this data, then you would undermine the whole climate change story and even – perhaps – the rationale for cutting Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions.
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Haines tribute speeches to open parliament, but Labor mustn’t overlook broader causes of boiling anger | Josh Butler.
Poverty, health and dislocation are fuelling political anger. Labor can’t ignore this in response to alleged attack on Indi MP Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Federal parliament will commence on Monday morning with speeches paying tribute to Helen Haines. It should be a unifying, bipartisan moment for an increasingly febrile, unpleasant political bubble. Our political representatives talk of turning down temperatures and being kinder, but the challenge is whether they will actually change their own behaviour – not just hector their opponents to do so.
- ABC News Australia, 7 hours ago: Hand-delivered death threat, being spat at among abuse ACT politicians cop.
ACT politicians speak about the abuse, threats and intimidation they've regularly been subjected to, following the attack on federal independent MP Helen Haines.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
